extracted.intended_audience: college business-school instructors, business communication teachers, and educators developing curriculum/units on proposal writing
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and delivering a unit or course that teaches undergraduate business students how to plan, write, evaluate, and defend business and research proposals. Emphasizes both the mechanics of persuasive, factual proposals and the research/design elements that make them executable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal as an initial planning step
rubrics_metrics.description: “The preparation of the proposal can be thought of as the initial planning step in the research process… will not only enhance one’s chances of getting the cold cash but will also improve the quality of the research.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat proposal writing as substantive project planning, not merely salesmanship. Avoid the anti-pattern of a hastily drawn proposal detached from the research process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin in problem recognition and clear problem statement
rubrics_metrics.description: All reports must have their origin in the recognition of a problem or a need; proposals should state problems and hypotheses in terms intelligible to those who are not sophisticated in the area of proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the proposal articulates a clear, significant problem/need and frames hypotheses or research questions in plain language for non-specialist reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation to sponsor/program guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt a model proposal to the specific guidelines of the particular program or unit which support or approval is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess conformity to sponsor formatting, required sections, length limits, and stated priorities. Failure to follow sponsor guidelines is a common grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include detailed procedures, facilities, personnel, schedules, and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate probable procedures, available facilities, personnel, time schedules, estimated costs, etc., to a believable, persuasive, factual, executable standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that methods are concrete and implementable, that facilities and personnel are identified, timelines are realistic, and cost estimates are justified and credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vary form by complexity, length, and intended readers
rubrics_metrics.description: The necessity for varying the form of proposals in line with their complexity, their length, and the readers for whom they are intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor level of technical detail, structure, and presentation to the proposal’s complexity and the knowledge/background of the reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to principles of effective communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance of adhering to all principles of effective communication in writing proposals (organization, clarity, correct grammar, appropriate vocabulary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess prose quality: logical organization, clear transitions, correct grammar, precise vocabulary, and readability. A proposal should be attractive, interesting, and grammatically correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be persuasive yet grounded in factual evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: In business contexts the proposal is a sales document—persuasive to a degree but depending heavily on its factual information for competitive success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance persuasive framing with verifiable facts, data, and realistic claims. Avoid over‑salesmanship unsupported by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize types and purposes of proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Know various types of proposals and the purposes, similarities, and dissimilarities of each, and identify the major components of a research proposal, their function and criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate awareness of solicited vs. unsolicited proposals, internal vs. external proposals, technical vs. business proposals, and adapt content accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-evaluation and peer critique aimed at acceptance likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate one’s own proposals in terms of their potential success in gaining acceptance, as well as in terms of 'correct' writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reviewer-perspective checklists and peer review exercises. Activities include written critiques, acting as reviewers, and defending critiques orally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare complete individual-initiated proposals containing standard parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare individual-initiated proposals that contain most of the standard parts of proposals and are superior examples of effective written communication techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess presence and quality of standard sections (title, abstract/summary, problem statement, objectives, methodology, timeline, budget, personnel, references) and overall cohesiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: State objectives, think creatively and analytically, organize persuasively
rubrics_metrics.description: Think creatively, analytically, intuitively; organize thoughts logically, interestingly and persuasively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the intellectual originality of the approach, clarity of objectives, and logical persuasiveness of the argument linking problem to proposed methods and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write for non-specialist understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: State problems and hypotheses in terms intelligible to those who are not sophisticated in the area of proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for excessive jargon, provide necessary explanation or definitions, and ensure the proposal communicates significance to lay or managerial reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary knowledge of research methods (sampling, statistics, questionnaires)
rubrics_metrics.description: An elementary knowledge of sampling techniques, statistics, and questionnaire construction useful to the proposal writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the chosen methods (sampling frame, analytic approach, measurement instruments) are appropriate and described at a competent, implementable level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective use of library and secondary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the library more effectively and make library assignments that force students to use a wide variety of secondary sources of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate literature review completeness, relevance of cited sources, and ability to synthesize secondary data to support need and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to read, synthesize, and abstract research reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Have students read several research reports and synthesize these reports in the form of either a descriptive or informative abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess summarization skills, accurate identification of main findings, and ability to convert full reports into concise abstracts that capture purpose, methods, and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral presentation and defense of proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Have each student (or selected students) orally present and defend before the class a proposal that he has written; require distribution of copies in advance and written critiques by peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity of oral defense, ability to answer reviewer questions, responsiveness to critique, and quality of written defenses and revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize proposals as blueprints for research
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive detailed proposals serve as a blueprint or guideline for the research activity, enabling the researcher to 'stay on course toward his objective.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the proposal gives sufficient procedural detail and checkpoints so that the proposed work can be executed and monitored against stated objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand duties and responsibilities of proposal preparers and evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: The duties and responsibilities of those who prepare proposals and the necessity for being able to evaluate proposals submitted by others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate understanding of ethical, managerial, and practical obligations (accurate budgeting, honest claims, disclosure of limitations) and the ability to critically appraise others’ proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop attitude: appreciation of proposal importance and resilience to rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop recognition of the important function proposals perform and the appreciation that not all proposals—even well‑written ones—can be accepted; a certain number of rejections must be taken in stride.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess students’ reflective understanding of the role of proposals in business/education/government and their readiness to iterate after rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate data collection methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the relative merits of mail interviews, telephone interviews, observations, and mail surveys and select collection devices appropriate to objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate justification for chosen data collection technique(s), discussion of their strengths/limitations, and appropriateness to research questions and population.
